items.evidence: All 24 sign block models in the vanilla 26.1.2 client jar are particle-only (no elements, no parent): models/block/oak_sign.json is {"textures": {"particle": "minecraft:block/oak_planks"}}; every sign blockstate points at its per-wood model; NO template_sign*.json files exist in the 26.1.2 jar. Vanilla draws the board in the BE renderer: AbstractSignRenderer declares abstract getSignModel(S)/getSignSprite(WoodType) + submitSign (javap), StandingSignRenderer/HangingSignRenderer implement them with createSignModel/createSignLayer; BlockEntityRenderers registers SIGN + HANGING_SIGN (javap -c). The port assumes the opposite: block_entity_render.rs:366 ('the boards are block models'), :1010-1011 ('Sign boards and beds are block models in the terrain mesh'), block_entity_cem.rs:11-12; Kind::Sign (:367-371) carries text layout only and the only sign drawing code is sign_text_calls (:662). With particle-only block models the mesher emits nothing for the board, so a placed sign shows floating text only. Sign ITEMS are unaffected (flat generated sprites in vanilla too). block_entity_render.rs and block_entity_cem.rs are byte-identical to 26.1.1's. Reproduces the 26.1.1 item with fresh 26.1.2 evidence.
items.title: Sign boards are not rendered: placed signs show floating text only

items.evidence: audio_harness.require_sounds() (tools/audio_harness.py:35-37) exits unless .local/horizon-client/26.1.2/assets/minecraft/sounds.json exists. The file is absent: the prepared .local (Batch 12's prepare run, exit 0) has a complete assets/minecraft/ tree but no sounds.json and no sounds/ directory anywhere in .local; it is also absent from the client jar (ships only in the asset index). Root cause is the prepare flow: horizon-prepare --prepare runs prepare_with_progress only; sounds need the separate 'horizon-prepare sounds' subcommand (main.rs:240) or --complete (:276-282). Runtime: SoundRegistry::load (sound_events.rs:262-287) silently skips a missing sounds.json per namespace (:280-282), so the registry is empty and every event resolves to Sound::empty(). All 6 audio_harness drivers gate-fail (sound_event, ambient_sound, music, situational_music, sound_engine, audio_attributes) and are oracle-blocked too (B10-O04). The wiring spec itself is clean (1,902 events vs 1,902 registry events; only the intentionally_empty sentinel and the chicken_picky.step orphan differ). sound_events.rs, horizon-prepare/src/main.rs and tools/audio_harness.py are byte-identical to 26.1.1's. Reproduces the 26.1.1 item.
items.title: No sounds.json in the prepared 26.1.2 resources: the game is silent and 6 audio drivers cannot run

items.evidence: Placed: vanilla 26.1.2 models/block/bed.json is particle-only and every bed blockstate points at it; no template_bed_head/foot or per-colour bed models in the jar. BedRenderer draws the whole bed (createHeadLayer/createFootLayer, submitPiece), registered for BlockEntityType.BED (javap -c; minecraft:bed IS a 26.1.2 BE type). The port has no Bed kind (block_entity_render.rs Kind enum :322-371, classify() falls to Kind::None :593, zero 'Bed' mentions in the file), so placed beds are invisible. Items: the minecraft:bed special decode arm is absent (item_model/special.rs:91-146 has no bed arm) and there is no bed draw path (item_render/special.rs has zero 'bed' mentions). SpecialModel::decode returns 'unknown special model type', propagating via ? (item_model.rs:555, ClientItem::decode :372-375), so all 16 bed items fail decode. Vanilla renders bed items via minecraft:composite of two minecraft:special nodes (bed, head + foot), and SpecialModelRenderers.bootstrap registers bed among 16 special types (javap -c). The standing_sign/hanging_sign decode arms are also absent but no bundled item uses those specials (exhaustive scan of all 1,506 item definitions). Covers two gap checks: placed beds + special-model decoder coverage. Bed sleep-height form is NOT a defect (Batch 3: shape-measured height coincides with vanilla's flat 0.6875). All cited files byte-identical to 26.1.1's. Reproduces the 26.1.1 item.
items.title: Beds are invisible when placed, AND bed items fail to decode (inherited from 26.1.1)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2 AnimationUtils.animateZombieArms (javap -c, client jar) RETURNS EARLY when the zombie isBaby && mainHandItemStack != EMPTY — a baby holding an item gets no zombie-arm animation at all. The 26.1.2 tree has the 26.2 form (mobs/anim.rs:638-656): let raise = !s.baby || !h.holding — a baby holding an item takes the raise=false branch, which LOWERS the arms with a flipped y-rotation. items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2 has NO SwingState/SwingDescription classes (0 jar entries). It swings on plain fields (swinging/swingTime/swingingArm/attackAnim/oAttackAnim), void swing(InteractionHand[, boolean]), private getCurrentSwingDuration() reading the swinging arm item's getSwingAnimation().duration() live with haste/fatigue adjustment, updateSwingTime() resetting at the duration so attackAnim never reaches 1.0, and restart gate !swinging || swingTime >= duration/2 || swingTime < 0 (all javap -c, server jar). The 26.1.2 tree carries the 26.3 form (first_person.rs:488-514: SwingDescription/SwingState, plus probe + oracle — the oracle carries 20 errors on exactly this). Observable differences: the port holds attackAnim at 1.0 an extra tick, allows restart at ticks==0 where vanilla blocks it, and caches the duration. Neither tree reads the swing_animation data component from items (only spears via Kinetic::attack_animation get non-DEFAULT), but no bundled item carries one, so that gap is unobservable. The packet half is B10-G11. first_person.rs is byte-identical to 26.1.1's. Reproduces the 26.1.1 item with fresh 26.1.2 evidence.
items.title: First-person swing uses the 26.3 SwingState state machine vanilla 26.1.2 does not have (holds 1.0 an extra tick, restart gate differs, duration cached)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2 LocalPlayer.swing(InteractionHand) calls AbstractClientPlayer.swing(hand) then UNCONDITIONALLY sends ServerboundSwingPacket(hand) (javap -c, javap-localplayer.txt:677-689); the server's handleAnimate (javap-sgpli.txt:4935-4951, same line numbers as 26.1.1 — the 26.1.2 ServerGamePacketListenerImpl change touched handleAttack, not handleAnimate) resets last-action time and swings the player, broadcasting to trackers. SwingSource is three-valued (NONE/CLIENT/SERVER, no PREDICTED, no shouldSwing). The 26.1.2 tree's swing_hand (game/hand.rs:195-216) sends NOTHING (the Serverbound import is gone too). swing_hand is the shared funnel for first-person clicks, remote_use native interactions, and all swing_arm() callers. Only the 3 explicit S::Swing sends in remote_start_attack/remote_continue_attack remain (remote.rs:9900, :10019, :10026). So attack swings still reach other players but item-use swings (place, use, interact) do not — the server never receives the packet, handleAnimate never runs, and the server-side guest state never records the swing (lan_actions.rs:2474 handler). Game::send is a no-op when remote is None (remote.rs:1641-1656), so the removal hits exactly the window/remote client. Multiplayer/LAN-only visibility; single-player unaffected. hand.rs and remote.rs are byte-identical to 26.1.1's. Reproduces the 26.1.1 item with fresh 26.1.2 evidence.
items.title: Item-use swings never reach other players: swing_hand no longer sends ServerboundSwingPacket (attack swings still send)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2 MultiPlayerGameMode.startDestroyBlock plays NOTHING (0 'Sound' occurrences); continueDestroyBlock plays ONLY the hit sound on destroy ticks 0, 4, 8, ... (destroyTicks % 4.0 == 0, BLOCKS, (volume+1)/8, pitch*0.5) — no particle at any point (addBreakingBlockEffect: 0 occurrences in the class). LevelEventHandler has NO 2019/2020 cases. The 26.1.2 tree: remote_mining's start calls breaking_block_effects(hit.pos, hit.face, true) (remote.rs:8180 — hit sound + crack at START), the continue branch plays NOTHING locally, and the server sends 2019 every dig tick + 2020 every fourth tick (game.rs:5294/:5306 -> destroy_progress_event, block_breaking.rs:100-107). Correction to Batch 8's claim: the port's server DOES send 2019/2020 — tick_mining runs for LAN guests (lan_actions.rs:4341) and the window player in default single-player IS a guest of its integrated server (remote.rs:1378; game.rs:5567 routes remote clients through tick_remote, never tick_local_hand). Net: closed loop hears a sound at START (one tick early) then roughly every fourth tick via 2020; against a vanilla 26.1.2 server the digger hears one mistimed sound at START then silence for the whole dig. Crack particles are B8-G09's half, not minted here. All cited files byte-identical to 26.1.1's. Reproduces the 26.1.1 item with fresh 26.1.2 evidence.

items.evidence: Vanilla passes the SoundSource as a parameter at each play site: Shearable.shear(level, source, stack) takes BLOCKS from the dispenser (tryShearEntity) and PLAYERS from player shearing; LevelEventHandler case 3003 plays the wax-on sound on BLOCKS. The port's Audio::play (audio.rs:1828 -> play_seeded :1978) derives the source from the event name via settings::sound_source (settings.rs:18-90, a prefix heuristic) — it can never express a source that depends on the caller. Verified instances: dispenser shear sounds play on NEUTRAL (sheep, mooshroom, snow golem, copper golem) or HOSTILE (bogged — in the heuristic's HOSTILE list) instead of BLOCKS; the wax-on sound plays on PLAYER (item. prefix) instead of BLOCKS. The heuristic happens to match where the name's prefix matches the context (potion break -> NEUTRAL, digging hit -> BLOCKS, beehive shear -> BLOCKS). Correction to the 26.1.1 report's 'used only by /playsound' note: Audio::play_on (audio.rs:2026) already has four game-code callers routing around the heuristic where it would be wrong — portal travel on AMBIENT (game.rs:4445), air-bubble pop on PLAYERS (game.rs:6147), projectile sounds on NEUTRAL (creatures.rs:5142, with a comment that the name heuristic would be wrong), ominous item spawner warning on NEUTRAL (ominous_item_spawner.rs:117) — plus a unit test (audio.rs:2182). The plumbing exists and is used; the shear and wax sites just don't use it. audio.rs, settings.rs and dispenser.rs are byte-identical to 26.1.1's. Audibility caveat: inaudible at default volumes (all sliders 1.0); bites when the user adjusts a category volume. Reproduces the 26.1.1 item (shared with 26.1).
items.title: Sound categories come from the event NAME, not the call site: shear and wax-on sounds land on the wrong volume slider (shared with 26.1)

source: docs/PARITY-SWEEP.md §4 Batch 10 — checks only, no fixes. Scope: models, block-entity rendering, screens, sound wiring, options; 50 drivers + static checks. 26.1.2 run: oracle status from the measured Batch 0 table only (no import-level check — the 26.2 run's B10 failure was not repeated); every 26.1.1 verdict re-verified fresh against 26.1.2's own jar/data + tree, with a diff against versions/26.1.1/ for every verdict change; report completeness verified by reading the tail before reporting.
systemic_note: Four systemic points. (1) THE DELTA PORT INHERITED 26.1.1'S DEFECTS WHOLESALE: vanilla changed nothing in scope between 26.1.1 and 26.1.2 (0 classes added/removed, asset index 30 byte-identical), the crate diff is 24 files with none in the B10 regression sites, and 16 of the 17 26.1.1 items reproduce with fresh 26.1.2 evidence. (2) 26.1.2 predates several 26.2/26.3 APIs the oracles assume — the Hud class split out of Gui, the EntityTypes holder move, FirstPersonHandsAndItems, UvMapping, renderpearl, shadeDirectionOverride, the SwingState/SwingDescription classes — so the oracle families fail with 26.1.1-identical causes (39 failing in-scope oracles recorded, 36 by the 26.1.1 counting convention); the Batch 0 table has zero deviations vs 26.1.1 across all 391 oracles. (3) Sound categories are derived from the event NAME, not the call site (G15) — a systemic audio-plumbing gap shared with 26.1 and 26.1.1, visible wherever vanilla's source is context-dependent (dispenser vs player shearing, event vs item-code wax). (4) METHOD LESSON from the G04 correction: a 'no port equivalent' claim needs a search over the whole render path (game.rs geometry calls), not just the Kind enum — the BE renderer file is not where this port draws half its block entities; the 26.1.1 run's file-scoped search minted a gap that never existed.
